items.summary: If this is real, this is stupendously fast growth.
items.body: If this is real, this is stupendously fast growth.

comments.text: diamonds aren't measured though. only the black dots are real, the rest is someone's estimate
comments.text_zh: 不过钻石并没有被测量。只有黑点是真实的，其余都是某人的估算。

comments.text: You're mixing up being worse with a slower rate of progress. That data is consistent with 2 month doubling times.
comments.text_zh: 你把“变得更差”和“进步速度变慢”搞混了。那些数据与两个月翻倍的时间是一致的。

comments.text: This only applies to well-specified, verifiable benchmark tasks. On messier AI R&D tasks progress is much slower. For example in this OpenAI report time horizons are < 30 minutes at 80% reliability. https://t.co/mze7nzzl32
comments.text_zh: 这只适用于定义明确、可验证的基准任务。在更混乱的AI研发任务上，进展要慢得多。例如在这份OpenAI报告中，80%可靠性下的时间跨度不到30分钟。https://t.co/mze7nzzl32

comments.text: so the biggest impact lands on recursive self-improvement, right?
comments.text_zh: 所以最大的影响落在递归自我改进上，对吧？

comments.text:
@paulg, this was entirely predictable.

If you didn't predict this there is something entirely off about your model of reality. I and most of my team lives off-grid already due to this year's predictable cybersecurity crisis.

It gets worse from here on out.

Unless we stop https://t.co/kjt9JOdkAj
comments.text_zh:
@paulg，这完全是可以预见的。

如果你没预见到这一点，那你的现实模型就有根本性的问题。由于今年可预见的网络安全危机，我和我的大部分团队已经离网生活了。

从这里开始只会更糟。

除非我们停止 https://t.co/kjt9JOdkAj

comments.text: METR grew exponentially fast, but the recent numbers are based off AECI (which is less abstract).
comments.text_zh: METR 增长得极快，但最近的数字是基于 AECI（没那么抽象）得出的。

comments.text: Growth that fast is also when the infra bill and the attack surface quietly double overnight. Fun problem to have though.
comments.text_zh: 增长那么快的时候，也正是基础设施账单和攻击面在一夜之间悄悄翻倍的时候。不过，这算是个幸福的烦恼。

comments.text: The scariest part of the METR graph isn't the slope. It's that most companies still plan like it's flat. What's the first job you think it eats?
comments.text_zh: METR 图表最吓人的地方不是斜率。而是大多数公司仍然按平坦的曲线来做规划。你觉得它最先吃掉哪个岗位？

comments.text: Worth remembering the headline line is at 50 percent success. The 80 percent horizon is a lot shorter, and that's closer to what you'd actually hand off without checking.
comments.text_zh: 值得记住的是，那个头条数字是50%成功率。80%的视野要短得多，而那更接近你实际不检查就直接交付的水平。

comments.text:
IDK I think progress on less verifiable tasks has been slower than very verifiable tasks.

In general data on this is very limited, and this OpenAI data covers a very short time period (and based on their data it looks like progress slowed around May 2026), but I think many
comments.text_zh:
我不知道，我觉得在不太可验证的任务上的进展比非常可验证的任务要慢。

总的来说，这方面的数据非常有限，而且这份OpenAI数据覆盖的时间段很短（根据他们的数据，进展似乎在2026年5月左右放缓了），但我认为许多

items.summary: I asked a group of experienced watchmakers what golden age movements they'd bet on to perform best today. Their consensus was Omega, for both automatics (the 55x/56x family) and manual winds (the 30T2…
items.body: I asked a group of experienced watchmakers what golden age movements they'd bet on to perform best today. Their consensus was Omega, for both automatics (the 55x/56x family) and manual winds (the 30T2 family).

comments.text:
A group of watchmakers actually agreeing on something.

That's the real golden age movement.
comments.text_zh:
一群制表师居然真的在某件事上达成了一致。

这才是真正的黄金时代运动。

comments.text: you can open the back and see how the whole thing works. try that with your phone
comments.text_zh: 你可以打开后盖看看整个东西是怎么运作的。拿你的手机试试看

comments.text: Did anyone make a case for the Longines 30L, or was it Omega all the way?
comments.text_zh: 有人为浪琴30L辩护吗，还是全程都是欧米茄？

comments.text: Omega’s 55x survives a marathon dive and a boardroom meeting—proof that a ‘golden age’ design still outpaces newer, fragile calibers.
comments.text_zh: 欧米茄的 55x 既能扛过马拉松式潜水，也能撑过董事会会议——这证明“黄金时代”的设计依然胜过更新、更脆弱的机芯。

comments.text: 565那个拉出快调日期的设计现在看都超前 😼‌⁡
Were they betting on accuracy today or on how easy parts are to find? those feel like pretty different bets
comments.text_zh: 他们赌的是当下的精度，还是零件有多容易找到？这两者感觉是相当不同的赌注。

comments.text: omega’s coaxial tech means less friction, so even a 30t2 from the ’70s still keeps time better than many modern “new” calibers.
comments.text_zh: 欧米茄的同轴技术意味着更少的摩擦，所以即便是 70 年代的 30t2，走时依然比许多现代“新”机芯更准。

comments.text: Serviceability decades later is the underrated moat in mechanical watches. A movement is only as good as the parts supply and the watchmakers who can still work on it.
comments.text_zh: 几十年后仍可维修，是机械表被低估的护城河。机芯的好坏，取决于零件供应和还能修它的制表师。

comments.text: The Seamasters from the 60s - 90s are beautiful
comments.text_zh: 60年代到90年代的海马系列很美

comments.text: Omega getting the nod is safe, but I'd bet on Seiko's modern engines if you want something with actual longevity in this market. Those 30T2 movements are solid workhorses though.
comments.text_zh: 欧米茄获得认可很稳妥，但如果你想在这个市场上有真正的长久性，我会押注精工的现代机芯。不过那些30T2机芯确实是可靠的主力。

translation.summary: 我问了一群经验丰富的制表师，他们认为如今哪些黄金时代机芯表现最佳。他们的共识是欧米茄，无论是自动上链（55x/56x 系列）还是手动上链（30T2 系列）。
translation.body: 我问了一群经验丰富的制表师，他们认为如今哪些黄金时代机芯表现最佳。他们的共识是欧米茄，无论是自动上链（55x/56x 系列）还是手动上链（30T2 系列）。
translation.label: 机器翻译

items.summary: for scale that is a 52m/171ft/15 story tall giant rocket flipping through the air and landing ready for reuse projected to lower payload launch cost from $2000/kg to $200/kg. reusability maybe the mos…
items.body:
for scale that is a 52m/171ft/15 story tall giant rocket flipping through the air and landing ready for reuse

projected to lower payload launch cost from $2000/kg to $200/kg. reusability maybe the most important advancement in spaceflight likely in our lifetimes…. and THERE WERE FREAKING HORSES running in the foreground just to make it more epic lol

comments.text: people watched a 15 story rocket flip through the air, land itself and then went back to their phones. we get used to miracles in about a week
comments.text_zh: 人们看着一栋 15 层楼高的火箭在空中翻转、自行着陆，然后转头继续刷手机。我们对奇迹的适应大概只需要一周

comments.text: https://t.co/57MbqSbHFm
watching a 15-story stainless steel building parallel park itself makes my weekend coding bugs feel embarrassing. $200/kg changes the math for everything
comments.text_zh: 看着一栋 15 层楼高的不锈钢建筑自己侧方停车，让我周末写代码的 bug 都显得尴尬了。每公斤 200 美元会改变一切的计算

comments.text: if it really gets down to $200/kg that changes a lot
comments.text_zh: 如果真能降到每公斤 200 美元，那会改变很多事

comments.text: Fifteen storeys of rocket doing a backflip and landing ready to go again. Reusability turns rockets from fireworks into aircraft.
comments.text_zh: 一栋十五层楼高的火箭在空中后空翻，然后稳稳落地、准备再次出发。可复用性把火箭从烟花变成了飞机。

comments.text:
You don’t need faster horses!

You need flipping rockets!

In just over 100 years.
comments.text_zh:
你需要的不是更快的马！

你需要的是能翻转的火箭！

就在短短 100 多年间。

comments.text: 10x cost drops in core infrastructure always break people's brains at first. Same thing happened with bandwidth, compute, and now orbit
comments.text_zh: 核心基础设施成本下降 10 倍，一开始总会让人脑子转不过来。带宽、算力，如今是轨道，都是同样的过程

comments.text: We got reusable rockets before reusable CI caches
comments.text_zh: 我们还没用上可复用的 CI 缓存，就先有了可复用火箭

comments.text: Thanks for doing the scale math. And if $2,000 a kilo really drops to $200, a lot more small hardware teams get to fly.
comments.text_zh: 感谢你做了规模上的计算。而如果每公斤 2000 美元真能降到 200 美元，那会有更多小型硬件团队有机会飞上天。

comments.text: operations tempo is the constraint now. doesn't matter if you can reuse it if turnaround kills your economics. that's the hard part
comments.text_zh: 现在真正的制约是运营节奏。就算你能复用，如果周转时间拖垮了经济性，那也没用。这才是最难的部分

translation.summary: 作为参照，那是一枚 52 米/171 英尺/15 层楼高的巨型火箭在空中翻转，然后着陆准备复用 预计将把有效载荷发射成本从每公斤 2000 美元降至每公斤 200 美元。可复用性或许是我们有生之年太空飞行中最重要的进步……而且前景里居然还有几匹该死的马在跑，就为了让画面更史诗一点，哈哈

comments.text: 100k already?? That's insane
comments.text_zh: 已经 10 万了？？太疯狂了

comments.text: Congrats. Best conference! 🤘🏻
comments.text_zh: 恭喜。最棒的会议！ 🤘🏻

comments.text: which part got the most questions in chat? curious if people are still stuck on context files or have moved on to reviewing what the agent wrote
comments.text_zh: 聊天里哪一部分问题最多？很好奇大家是还卡在上下文文件上，还是已经转到审查代理写出来的东西了

comments.text: Practices beat landscape for us too. 45 days of two founders + coding agents on telecom tools: what mattered wasn't the model, it was ~6,800 automated tests and a human sign-off before anything public. Any talks on evals outside pure software?
comments.text_zh: 对我们来说，实践同样比全景扫描更重要。两个创始人加上编程代理，用 45 天做电信工具：真正重要的不是模型，而是大约 6800 个自动化测试，以及任何对外发布前的人工签字。有没有纯软件之外、关于评测的分享？

comments.text: coding agent practices is the one I'd watch. would love a segment on what agents get wrong on security by default, like putting keys client side because it "works"
comments.text_zh: 编程代理实践是我会看的那一期。很希望能有一段讲代理在安全上默认会犯哪些错，比如把密钥放在客户端，就因为这样“能跑”

comments.text: Coding agent content is undefeated right now.
comments.text_zh: 编程代理内容现在简直无敌。

comments.text: i run a one-person company with agents doing the building. what i'd love covered is the failure side, cost blowups and what to do when an agent confidently breaks something. any day planned on that?
comments.text_zh: 我一个人开公司，建造工作交给代理做。我很希望能讲到失败的一面，比如成本爆炸，以及代理很自信地把东西搞坏时该怎么办。有安排哪一天讲这个吗？

comments.text: Practical agent talks give viewers something to try after the stream, which seems like a useful signal beyond reach. Do you track which sessions lead people to reproduce a workflow or return with implementation questions? That could help choose the next deep dive.
comments.text_zh: 偏实践的代理分享能让观众在直播结束后有东西可试，这似乎是比曝光量更有用的信号。你会追踪哪些场次会让人去复现一个工作流，或带着实现问题再回来吗？这有助于选择下一次深挖的方向。

comments.text: Do these practical sessions get most of their views live, or do the replays do the heavy lifting?
comments.text_zh: 这些实践场次的播放量，主要来自直播，还是回放在扛大头？

comments.text: Live wins here because agent practices go stale in weeks; a writeup from last month already describes a different set of tools. Would love a segment on failures too, watching an agent go wrong live teaches more than another polished demo.
comments.text_zh: 直播在这里更合适，因为代理实践几周就会过时；上个月的一篇总结描述的已经是另一套工具了。也很希望有一期讲失败，看着代理现场出错，比又一场打磨过的演示更有收获。

translation.summary: 另外，第一天的直播以有史以来最快的速度突破了 10 万观看。讲编程 Agent 的实践与格局，依然是我们做过最强的形式，也是我做过的、产品市场契合度最高的方向，没有之一。https://t.co/cM43xYQLMT
translation.body: 另外，第一天的直播以有史以来最快的速度突破了 10 万观看。讲编程 Agent 的实践与格局，依然是我们做过最强的形式，也是我做过的、产品市场契合度最高的方向，没有之一。https://t.co/cM43xYQLMT
